summary:
### TL;DR
- **`pull_request_target` default policy enforcement moves to December 2, 2026.** It was November 2. Public repos that relied on the default policy before GA will have `pull_request_target`-triggered workflows blocked from that date. Use the extra month to review policy insights. ([docs commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/e8090f5f830a6dd6faf638181f002e3cf4b13d9d))
- **Public monitoring for leaked secrets gains triage tools** (public preview, GHEC). New features are dismiss/reopen, an activity timeline, always-on validity checks, a REST API and an enterprise webhook. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-23-public-monitoring-adds-triage-validity-api-and-webhooks))
- **Enterprise installations for GitHub Apps are now GA.** New permissions cover 2FA, IP allowlists, rulesets, verified domains and access restrictions, so more automation can move off classic PATs. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-23-enterprise-installations-for-github-apps-generally-available))
- **An EMU SCIM bug deleted about 12,285 accounts** between June 1 and June 13, 2026, instead of suspending them. GitHub has restored the records and no action is needed. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-23-emu-deletions-fix))

### Action required
- **`pull_request_target` default policy, December 2, 2026.**
  - **Who:** public repositories with no applicable Actions event policy that were using the default `pull_request_target` policy before GA.
  - **Current state:** the default policy runs in evaluate mode. Runs still proceed, and policy insights show which runs would be blocked.
  - **What happens on the deadline:** affected workflows will fail with a policy error.
  - **What to do:** review policy insights before the deadline. Then either harden and explicitly allow the workflows you need, or migrate them. ([Securely using pull_request_target](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target), [About Actions policies](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/about-actions-policies))
- **Legacy GitHub app for Microsoft Teams retires November 16.** It will be renamed "GitHub (deprecated)". To keep using Copilot in Teams, install the consolidated GitHub app. If you already use the GitHub notifications app, update it to the latest version. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-23-turn-notifications-into-code-with-github-copilot-in-teams))

### Security improvements
- **Public monitoring alert management** ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-23-public-monitoring-adds-triage-validity-api-and-webhooks)):
  - **Triage:** you can dismiss alerts (as Dismissed or Fixed) or reopen them, with optional comments. Each alert has an activity timeline. You can filter by repository, committer, secret type, attribution method and state.
  - **Closing is not remediation:** closing an alert does not revoke the credential or remove it from the public repository.
  - **Validity checks:** supported secret types are checked continuously and marked Active, Inactive or Unknown, so you can prioritize live tokens.
  - **Integration:** use `GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/secret-scanning/public-monitoring-alerts` or the enterprise webhook `secret_scanning_public_monitoring_alert`.
  - **Licensing:** included at no extra cost with GitHub Advanced Security or GitHub Secret Protection.
- **GitHub Apps on enterprises (GA)** ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-23-enterprise-installations-for-github-apps-generally-available)):
  - **New permissions:** enterprise policies, bypass requests (read), settings, 2FA requirements, IP allowlists (enterprise and org), verifiable domains (enterprise and org), access restrictions and rulesets.
  - **Existing-permission gaps closed:** enterprise people and enterprise billing now support more APIs.
  - **Why it matters:** this is a path to replace classic PATs in admin automation.
  - **GHES:** coming in GHES 3.24.
- **EMU deletion incident, resolved** ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-23-emu-deletions-fix)):
  - **What happened:** a new deprovisioning path did not check whether an account was an EMU account. Accounts were deleted, and appeared as ghost users in issues, PRs and audit logs.
  - **Scope:** 76 of the affected accounts were active at the time.
  - **Checking whether you were hit:** look for `user.delete` events on EMU accounts in your audit log for June 1–13, 2026.
  - **Fix:** records were restored in October 2026 to their suspended and obfuscated state.
- **Copilot usage metrics `totals_by_client`** ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-23-usage-metrics-api-adds-usage-from-tools-like-opencode)):
  - **What it adds:** server-side request and token counts per client tool, such as OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex and the CLI.
  - **Governance use:** shows which tools use Copilot as their model provider.
  - **Caveat:** clients are identified by the integration ID they send. Treat the `client` field as a best-effort grouping, not a verified identity.

### Docs changes worth reading
- **`pull_request_target` enforcement date** ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/e8090f5f830a6dd6faf638181f002e3cf4b13d9d)): the enforcement date changed from November 2 to December 2, 2026, in three pages:
  - [Securely using pull_request_target](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target)
  - [About Actions policies](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/about-actions-policies)
  - [Control workflow execution](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/administer/control-workflow-execution)
- **Public monitoring alerts page** ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/b7f92867cb168fd07cd8b4e423e97deafcef77f9), [page](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/view-and-interpret-data/analyze-organization-data/viewing-public-monitoring-alerts)):
  - Retitled "Viewing and managing public monitoring alerts".
  - New section on dismissing and reopening alerts with optional comments, to keep the open list focused when alert volume is high.

changelog.title: Usage metrics API adds usage from tools like OpenCode
changelog.text: The Copilot usage metrics API now reports model usage from more of the tools your developers use with Copilot, including tools like OpenCode that weren’t previously captured in your reports. A new totals_by_client array is available in the enterprise, organization, enterprise-user, and organization-user 1-day and 28-day reports. What’s new Each totals_by_client entry represents one client and includes: client : The tool that sent the requests, such as opencode , claude_code , codex , zed , copilot_cli , github_app , cloud_agent , code_review , vscode , or jetbrains . Unrecognized clients are grouped under other . request_count : The number of successful model requests from the client. session_count : The number of distinct sessions from the client. token_usage : Prompt tokens, output tokens, and average tokens per request. totals_by_model : The same request and token metrics broken down by model, with a model_selection_mode that shows whether the model was requested directly ( user_selected ), chosen by auto ( auto ), or chosen by the product ( product_selected ). Selection modes that aren’t reported individually yet appear as other , and values that can’t be normalized appear as unknown . Why this matters More developers now use Copilot as the model provider behind tools outside the IDE. Because those tools often don’t send editor telemetry, their usage was missing from totals_by_ide and hard to account for. Counting requests on the server closes that gap, so you can see which tools drive Copilot usage, compare request and token volume across them, and base tool support and governance decisions on real usage. This is different from agent app activity , which counts jobs started by agent apps such as Claude and Codex on GitHub. totals_by_client measures model traffic, meaning requests and tokens, from any tool that uses Copilot. Important notes Scope: Enterprise, organization, enterprise-user, and organization-user reports, in both 1-day and 28-day versions. In the aggregated 28-day reports, totals_by_client appears in each day_totals entry. Access: Available to enterprise owners and billing managers, organization owners, and anyone with a custom organization or enterprise role that grants the View Copilot Metrics permission. The Copilot usage metrics policy must be enabled. Copilot code review and Copilot cloud agent: Requests from these clients report product_selected because the product chooses the model. Copilot code review models are reported as unknown . Request counts: request_count counts model calls, not prompts. One prompt can trigger several model calls, so don’t compare this field directly with prompt or interaction counts. Client identification: Clients are identified by the integration ID they send with each request. Treat client as a best-effort grouping, not a verified identity. Backward compatibility: This change is additive. Existing fields are unchanged, and totals_by_client is an empty array when there is no usage to report. Visit the Copilot usage metrics API documentation to get started. The post Usage metrics API adds usage from tools like OpenCode appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Turn notifications into code with GitHub Copilot in Teams
changelog.text: The new GitHub app in Teams brings notifications and Copilot together, helping teams turn issues into fixes and ship code faster without leaving the conversation. Get notified in channels, group chats, or private chats, then @mention GitHub to turn updates into action. Turn an issue notification into a pull request Get notified: A bug report arrives in Teams. Take action: @github investigates the issue, fixes the bug, and creates a pull request. Review and ship: Your team reviews, tests, and merges the fix. Get started Explore the new GitHub app in Microsoft Teams , previously called GitHub notifications. If you already have GitHub notifications installed, update the app to the latest version. Your existing notification capabilities will continue to work. If you use the legacy GitHub app, which will be renamed “GitHub (deprecated)” and retired on November 16, install the consolidated GitHub app using the link above to continue using Copilot in Teams. In the consolidated app, mention @GitHub and follow any prompts to connect your GitHub account and select a repository. Join the discussion within the GitHub Community . The post Turn notifications into code with GitHub Copilot in Teams appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: EMU deletions fix
changelog.text: Between June 1 and June 13, 2026, some Enterprise Managed User accounts that were deprovisioned through SCIM were incorrectly deleted instead of being suspended and obfuscated as expected. As a result, affected users appeared as ghost users in issues, pull requests, and audit logs, rather than retaining their expected suspended and obfuscated user records within the enterprise. Who was affected This affected approximately 12,285 Enterprise Managed User accounts across multiple enterprises. Most affected accounts had already been suspended and hard-deprovisioned, which means they couldn’t be reprovisioned by design. A smaller group of 76 accounts were active at the time of deletion. How to tell if you were affected You were affected if your enterprise audit logs contain a user.delete event for an Enterprise Managed User account during the June 1 to June 13, 2026 window. If you do not see any such events in that window, your enterprise was not impacted. If you do see these events, no action is required from you. GitHub is restoring the affected accounts. What caused the issue On June 1, 2026, GitHub enabled a change that routed deprovisioning requests through a new path. That path didn’t correctly check whether the account was an Enterprise Managed User account, which caused the affected accounts to be deleted instead of following the expected suspend-and-obfuscate flow. GitHub contained the issue by disabling the affected path on June 13, 2026. What we’re doing to fix it We’ve made code changes to prevent this from happening again. We’ve also restored affected user records in October 2026. The restoration process returned affected accounts to their expected suspended and obfuscated state, preserving traceability and audit history within the enterprise. Enterprise owners don’t need to take any action. Hard-deprovisioned Enterprise Managed User accounts can’t be reprovisioned by design, so this issue doesn’t affect the reprovisioning workflow. The post EMU deletions fix appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Public monitoring adds triage, validity, API, and webhooks
changelog.text: Public monitoring now includes alert management capabilities like automatic validity checks to help you triage and remediate leaked secrets at scale. Alert management with dismissals, timelines, and filtering Always-on validity checks for supported secret types REST API and webhook support for public monitoring alerts Alert management Enterprises with public monitoring can now triage findings directly from the enterprise security dashboard: Dismiss and reopen alerts: Close alerts as Dismissed or Fixed , provide an optional comment explaining the decision, or reopen closed alerts if circumstances change. Activity timeline: Review an audit trail of all actions and state changes taken on an alert. Filter and sort: Filter the alert list by repository, committer, secret type, attribution method (membership or verified domain), and state (i.e., open or closed ) to focus on the exposures that matter most. Closing an alert updates its state for your enterprise. It does not revoke the exposed credential or remove it from the public repository. Always-on validity checks Public monitoring now automatically checks token validity on an ongoing basis for supported providers. Alerts display whether a credential is Active , Inactive , or Unknown , allowing security teams to quickly prioritize response for live tokens. REST API and webhook integration Bring public monitoring findings into your custom incident response pipelines: REST API: Enterprise admins and enterprise security managers can query attributed findings programmatically using GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/secret-scanning/public-monitoring-alerts . This returns alert metadata, secret type, attribution, and exposed locations. Enterprise webhooks: Subscribe to the secret_scanning_public_monitoring_alert webhook event at the enterprise level to receive real-time notifications whenever a newly detected leak is attributed to your organization. Eligibility and billing Public monitoring remains available in public preview for GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers, including GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. Enterprise admins and enterprise security managers can enable the feature and manage alert settings from the enterprise security dashboard. Public monitoring is included with your GitHub Advanced Security or GitHub Secret Protection license at no additional cost. Learn more Learn more about public monitoring and join the discussion in the GitHub Community . The post Public monitoring adds triage, validity, API, and webhooks appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Enterprise installations for GitHub Apps generally available
changelog.text: Installing GitHub Apps on your enterprise is now generally available. You can replace classic PATs with GitHub Apps in more of your enterprise and organization automation with the expanded API support detailed below. These new and expanded permissions are focused on governance, security, and administrative settings for your enterprise, with two gaps at the organization level also closed. What’s new for GitHub Apps Governance: Manage enterprise-level repository policies and rulesets as well as read delegated bypass requests. Security: Configure two-factor authentication requirements, verify domains, manage IP allowlists, and control enterprise access restrictions. Administration: Update enterprise profiles and manage both member privileges and repository access settings across the enterprise. New permissions and API coverage Choose the permissions your workflow needs in your GitHub App settings. Permission Access Newly supported APIs and GraphQL data Enterprise organization and repository policies Read/write Read policy fields on EnterpriseOwnerInfo . Update private repository forking , default repository permissions , repository visibility changes , repository creation , repository deletion , issue deletion , collaborator invitations , deploy keys , protected branch updates , dependency insights setting , organization projects setting , and repository projects . Enterprise bypass requests Read Read push-rule and repository-policy bypass requests . Enterprise settings Read/write Read enterprise data through EnterpriseOwnerInfo , including server installations and organization invitations. Update the enterprise profile . Read is required for access to the enterprise organization and repository policies. Enterprise two-factor authentication Read/write Read two-factor fields on EnterpriseOwnerInfo . Update two-factor requirements and disallowed authentication methods . Enterprise verifiable domains; organization verifiable domains Write Access VerifiableDomain s for enterprises or organizations. Enterprise IP allowlist; organization IP allowlist Read/write Access IpAllowListEntry and associated mutations to create, update, and delete entries on an enterprise or organization IP allowlist. Also toggle allowlist enforcement, trust of GitHub Apps, and user-level enforcement for Enterprise Managed Users. Enterprise access restrictions Write Enable or disable enterprise access restrictions . Enterprise repository rulesets Write Manage rulesets through the enterprise rules REST APIs and RepositoryRuleset in GraphQL . More coverage with existing permissions Some APIs and objects had gaps in their support for GitHub Apps. These fixes should unblock more automation scenarios with those permissions. Permission Access Newly supported APIs and GraphQL data Enterprise people Read/write Read EnterpriseRepositoryInfo , including repository details through EnterpriseOwnerInfo.outsideCollaborators . Add yourself to an organization with the owner or member role . Enterprise billing Write Update the member purchasing setting for the Marketplace. To get started, choose permissions for your GitHub App for the workflows you want to migrate. These updates will be available in GHES 3.24. For details on using GraphQL with a GitHub App, see Managing an enterprise account with GraphQL . To learn more about enterprise app installations, see Installing a GitHub App on your enterprise . The post Enterprise installations for GitHub Apps generally available appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
